title: Channels: sending, receiving, closing and ranging

videos.script: A goroutine cannot return a value to whoever started it. This lesson gives it a way back: the channel. {{send}} Two goroutines add up two lists and send their totals on one channel. Main receives twice. Each receive waits until a value arrives, so main needs no wait group and no sleep. Both totals land at two hundred milliseconds, because the two goroutines slept side by side. {{close}} Then the end of the data. Closing a channel says no more values are coming. Receives keep answering, with the zero value and a flag that says false. Sending after a close panics, and so does closing twice. So only the sender closes, once. {{range}} Last, the loop that ties it together. Range over a channel takes values until it is closed. Delete the close, and the loop waits forever for a word nobody will send. {{close-out}} Lesson 4 is about the meeting itself: when a send waits, and when it does not.
